# Sirach Chapter 36 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 36 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_036_page_001.jpg

---

36:1 Show us mercy, Lord God of all, and turn your gaze toward us.

36:2 Strike all the nations with terror.

36:3 Raise your mighty hand against foreign peoples; let them see your power at work.

36:4 Just as you revealed your holiness among us for all to see, now reveal your greatness among them for us to see.

36:5 Let them acknowledge you as we have — that there is no God but you, Lord.

36:6 Do it again: repeat your signs, work new wonders; let your hand and your mighty arm be shown to be glorious.

36:7 Unleash your anger; pour out your fury. Crush our enemies; wipe them out.

36:8 Bring the moment forward; honor your oath — and give your people reason to tell of what you have done.

36:9 Let burning wrath consume whatever is left. Let those who mistreat your people be destroyed.

36:10 Crush the heads of rulers who oppress us — the ones who say, "There's nobody equal to us."

36:11 Gather all the tribes of Jacob together and restore them to the inheritance they held in the beginning.

36:12 Lord, show mercy to the people who bear your name — to Israel, the nation you called your firstborn.

36:13 Have pity on the holy city, your Jerusalem — the place where you have set your dwelling.

36:14 Fill Zion with the news of your deeds; fill your temple with your glory.

36:15 Vindicate the people you made from the start, and bring to fulfillment what your prophets have spoken.

36:16 Give those who wait for you what they deserve, and prove your prophets right.

36:17 Hear the prayer of your servants. Bless your people as Aaron blessed them, so that everyone on earth will know you are the Lord God who endures forever.

36:18 The stomach is willing to take in any food, but some food is simply better than other food.

36:19 The palate knows the difference between meats; a discerning mind knows the difference between true and false words.

36:20 A dishonest heart brings grief; but the experienced person knows how to give it back as good as they got.

36:21 A man may find any woman acceptable, but there's a real difference between one woman and another.

36:22 There is nothing more desirable than a beautiful woman — her beauty puts a smile on her husband's face.

36:23 But if her tongue is also kind and gentle, then her husband is truly a man set apart from others.

36:24 A man who finds a wife has found something precious — a partner made for him, a steady support.

36:25 An unguarded field will be stripped bare; a man without a wife will wander restlessly and sigh.

36:26 Would you trust a bandit who slips from town to town? Of course not. Neither would you trust a man with no home, who ends up wherever the night finds him.
